Question B-006-010-001.

Why the correct answer is right: For practical quarter-wavelength verticals below 30 MHz, use length in metres = 71.3 / frequency in MHz. This is the quarter-wave partner to the 143/f half-wave estimate.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Divide 468 by the operating frequency in MHz": 468/f is the common half-wave dipole length in feet, not a quarter-wave length in metres.
- sourceIndex 2: "Divide 300 by the operating frequency in MHz": 300/f gives the approximate free-space full wavelength in metres. A quarter-wave vertical is about one quarter of that, with practical shortening.
- sourceIndex 3: "Divide 143 by the operating frequency in MHz": 143/f is the practical half-wave length in metres. A quarter-wave vertical uses half that constant, 71.3/f.
